description: Write a whole thread to a local file instead of returning it — for keeping, sharing, or reading a long conversation without loading it into the context. `markdown` (default): one section per message with From/To/Date/Subject and attachment names as inline code (never rendered as a link or image), sender authentication and the attachment list, and the body in a code fence that the message text cannot close (HTML-only mail is reduced to text). `json`: the parsed messages as get_thread returns them, HTML included. Both formats strip the same hidden characters (zero-width, bidi controls) as every tool result. Attachments are listed, not saved — use download_attachment for those. If MAILWARDEN_DOWNLOAD_DIR is set, destPath is resolved inside (and restricted to) that directory, as for attachments. The file holds mail text as the sender wrote it: untrusted content, now on disk. USE WHEN: the user wants a conversation saved or handed on, or a thread is too long to read in one piece. DO NOT USE: to read a thread (use get_thread). SIDE EFFECTS: writes a local file; never overwrites — an existing file gets a numeric suffix. The response's 'saved' field is the path actually used. Mailbox unchanged.
name: export_thread
